candidate_relations.reason: AMAN is a subtype of GBS. 'Guillain-Barré Syndrome' without further qualification is the parent category and lacks the required axonal motor specificity. The clinical picture (pure motor, ascending flaccid paralysis, areflexia, normal CSF protein, post-URI, no sensory loss) strongly favors AMAN over AIDP, so the unqualified parent label is insufficient.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: GBS is the parent syndrome encompassing AMAN, AMSAN, AIDP, and other variants; does not specify the axonal motor subtype

candidate_relations.reason: AIDP is a distinct subtype of GBS characterized by demyelination, whereas AMAN is an axonal motor variant. The two are incompatible subtypes within the GBS family; asserting 'Classical GBS (AIDP)' conflicts with the required AMAN designation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Classical GBS / AIDP is the demyelinating subtype, which conflicts with the axonal motor subtype (AMAN) that is the reference diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: ALS presents with mixed UMN/LMN signs, is chronic and progressive over months to years, and does not cause acute ascending flaccid paralysis with areflexia over days. This is a different diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ALS is a chronic neurodegenerative upper and lower motor neuron disease, entirely different from an acute post-infectious peripheral neuropathy

candidate_relations.reason: Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP) is the same entity as C002 and represents the demyelinating form of GBS. The reference diagnosis is AMAN, an axonal (non-demyelinating) motor variant, making AIDP an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: AIDP is the demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy subtype, conflicting with the axonal motor subtype AMAN

case_quality_flags: CSF protein is normal (33 mg/dL) and cell count is 1, which is atypical for classic GBS albuminocytologic dissociation but consistent with early AMAN; electrodiagnostic studies (NCS/EMG) are absent, which would be definitive for subtype classification
Anti-ganglioside antibodies (e.g., anti-GM1) not reported, which would further support AMAN diagnosis
